key_insight: In a morphoelastic burn-healing model, individual parameter variations mainly govern peak wound contraction, while higher-order interactions govern its timing and permanent contracture.
engineering_relevance: Scaling analysis supports neglecting chemotaxis and inertia, enabling a quasi-static formulation for computational modelling of burn-wound deformation.
method: Nondimensionalization and scaling analysis to simplify coupled biological–mechanical PDEs.
Finite-element variational inequalities in FEniCSx to enforce non-negativity.
Large-scale sensitivity analysis of contraction outcomes and solver stability.
evidence_signal: The framework was verified through numerical convergence studies and mass balances, with sensitivity analysis spanning nearly four million simulations.
watch_item: Solver stability depends on higher-order parameter interactions, particularly those involving equilibrium collagen density and signalling dynamics.
paper_title: Nondimensionalization, Variational Inequalities and Uncertainty Quantification in a Morphoelastic Model for Burn Injury Healing
